page: Microsoft Azure D4as_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine within the Dav6 family, powered by the AMD EPYC 9V74 processor based on the x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with multithreading enabled at a base clock speed of 3.7 GHz. Hardware caches include 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. It incorporates advanced instruction set extensions such as AVX-512 (supporting VNNI and BF16), hardware cryptography acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA-NI, as well as AMD SVM virtualization support.

The virtual machine features 16.0 GB of system memory, matching the standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio common in general-purpose configurations (4.0 GB per vCPU). The instance does not include bundled local instance storage, operating instead with attached remote storage volumes under Premium Storage capability. It includes zero bundled hardware accelerators and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, routing traffic through Azure hypervisor virtual networking interfaces.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-thread compute capabilities, ranking in the top 25% on stress-ng single-core (3079.08) and Geekbench single-core (1989.0) tests, as well as Geekbench text processing (2514.0). Multi-core compute performance remains in the middle 50% tier, with Geekbench multi-core reaching 4458.0 and PassMark CPU scoring 7534.96. Memory read throughput shows lower comparative performance, logging 37.99 GB/sec on large uncached read tests and 214.86 GB/sec on cached tests, which correlates with weaker outcomes in database operations (PassMark database score of 1929.19) and Redis SET throughput (5.9 million operations/second). Small-scale LLM inference on a 135M model handles 159.8 generation tokens/second, whereas a 7B parameter model operates slowly at 7.97 generation tokens/second.

Given its balanced CPU-to-memory density, strong single-core performance, and reliance on remote block storage, the D4as_v6 is suited for web serving, microservices, application backends, and standard text processing. Workloads requiring high memory bandwidth, dense database caching, or local NVMe storage profiles will experience throughput constraints.
description: Microsoft Azure D4as_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dav6 instance series. Configured with an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor operating at 3.7 GHz, it supplies 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores and 16.0 GB of memory, preserving a standard 1:4 compute-to-RAM ratio. Instruction support includes AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16, alongside AES and SHA-NI cryptographic instructions. The instance includes no bundled local storage or hardware accelerators, depending on remote Premium Storage volumes. In benchmarking, the D4as_v6 exhibits strong single-core execution speed and average multi-core efficiency, but shows reduced performance in uncached memory bandwidth, software compilation, and in-memory operations like Redis and relational database tests. It functions effectively for web serving, application logic, and microservices.
